questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Wanted to try living in London during my gap year, which was difficult because of covid. This was the perfect opportunity to fulfill this "dream".

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. I didn't really have any problems, information wise.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We received a lot of emails with information regarding visa and necessary information. We did receive a lot of information though, and it was a bit difficult to figure out whether it was necessary to read the emails or not.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very difficult. There is a lot of student accommodation available but it's all extremely expensive. I was lucky to get in touch with a friend of my co-worker.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Get in touch with KFUK early on to get cheap accommodation. Otherwise it's all about luck.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We weren't allowed to stay at campus because we were only there for half a year, even though there were rooms available.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
You could apply for courses for one week in the summer. I was able to make registrations twice during this period.
The registration would close after this week and be opened again one week before teaching started. Registration would be open for two weeks this time and after the two weeks are over, the classes you've got are locked in.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could write an email to someone at the campus, but during the first registration period she was very difficult to get in contact with as everyone was trying to get in contact with her.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very unsuccessful. Both my attempts got declined during the first registration period. This was because I was waiting to receive my grade from preliminary courses. As I was yet to pass the exams (because I wouldn't receive my grade for another two weeks) I couldn't apply for the courses I wanted. It's a first come first serve basis and the courses in economics gets filled quickly, so the courses I wanted weren't available when the registration period opened again and I had to settle for other courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get a prior approval from KU for at least 10 courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took one class with 2. year students and three courses with 3. year students. It was very easy to follow the courses compared to the difficulty in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar. Lectures and classes with a teachers assistant solving problem sets.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
History of economic thought
Economics of social issues
Macroeconomic policy
Health economics

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Economics of social issues was a very interesting subject and the teacher was very good.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of clubs, both athletic and non-athletic. There are also a few parties and tours to explore the city.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join some of the clubs, even if the sport doesn't interest you. This is by far the easiest way to meet people at the school.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See some football and go to the local pub.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: family easy, the uk is pretty similar to Denmark

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a club. The university doesn't really do anything to help the students socialise.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really anything.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The pub culture is great.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Join a club. Save up some money before the trip. Walk around in the city instead of taking the tube if you've got the time.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Contact KFUK to get cheap accommodation

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Trying something new.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Trying to socialise in the beginning, as I didn't know anyone.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Would be great if KU had let us know who the other people going to the same university are. The other people I met from KU was completely by accident.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
